candidates.title: FRA awards $1.24 billion for grade crossing projects
candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — The Federal Railroad Administration has awarded $1.24 billion for projects in 37 states under the Grade Crossing Elimination grant program. A total of 91 projects were selected from 264 applications, which sought funding totaling $4.9 billion. Program funding is from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act of 2021, which expires this year. Recipients must provide at least a 20% match. Texas had eight projects selected, the most of any state. California, Georgia, and Washington each had six projects selected. FRA Administrator David Fink said in a press release that the grants “will provide communities nationwide with funding to make highway-rail grade crossings safer and reduce the occurrence of blocked crossings. candidates.excerpt: Sidra Line will introduce a new container connection between Türkiye and St Petersburg. The carrier will operate the service under its Türkiye Russia Express (TRX) designation. candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — The National Mediation Board has formally authorized a representational election for Union Pacific dispatchers, which will determine if they will organize under the American Train Dispatchers Association, the union announced on Thursday, Oct. 29. Robinson said CN has delivered $120 million worth of productivity and efficiency gains this year, and that its “boots on the ground” sales efforts have generated $300 million in revenue to help offset the impact of U.S. tariffs and trade tensions. candidates.excerpt: Soaring tanker freight rates are taking an increasingly heavy toll on the world’s oil majors, with the latest quarterly results revealing billions of dollars in additional shipping-related liabilities, squeezed refining margins and losses on trading positions. Shell has disclosed a $5.4bn non-cash increase in its shipping lease liabilities during the third quarter, reflecting the extraordinary rise in tanker rates since the outbreak of the Middle East conflict. The accounting adjustment relates to index-linked vessel charters, which must be revalued using prevailing spot rates. candidates.excerpt: Kroll and StepStone launch private credit PIK indicators Kroll and StepStone Group have launched three new payment-in-kind (PIK) indicators to provide greater transparency into the use of non-cash interest in private credit markets. The indicators form part of the firms’ private credit benchmarks, covering more than 28,000 direct lending instruments, 18,000 deals and 13,000 borrowers, with historical data dating back to 2012. They measure PIK as a proportion of interest income, the percentage of loans with an active PIK component by deal count, and their share of outstanding principal. The indicators will also allow investors to compare PIK usage across geographies, sectors and borrower sizes. The launch comes as the firms’ data suggests PIK usage is moderating, with non-cash interest accounting for 2.86 per cent of interest income on loans originated globally over the previous 12 months, as of 10 October 2026. candidates.excerpt: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs. Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier, the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) said in earnings released after the close of markets. Core adjusted diluted earnings increased to 91 cents per share from 78 cents, while reported diluted earnings rose 3% to 74 cents from 72 cents. candidates.title: Greenbrier profit falls as railcar demand weighs on sales
candidates.excerpt: Greenbrier Cos. reported a sharp decline in quarterly profit and revenue as the freight-railcar manufacturer contended with weaker demand and facility-related costs. The Lake Oswego, Ore., company (NYSE: GBX) saw an increase in its order backlog and growth in its leasing fleet amid improving business conditions. The company said Monday that net earnings attributable to Greenbrier fell to $8.7 million, or 27 cents a diluted share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Aug. 31, from $36.8 million, or $1.16 a share, a year earlier. Revenue declined 22% to $591 million from $759.5 million. Excluding facility-rationalization costs, core earnings were 39 cents a share. The charges reduced quarterly earnings by 12 cents a share after tax and non-controlling interests. Revenue fell short of analysts’ expectations of about $605 million, while core earnings missed the 80-cent analysts’ consensus of MarketBeat.
